summary.headline: Yes for serving, search, agents and data; not yet for RL, multi-node training or framework parity.
summary.summary: Rust is the right choice when deployment simplicity, memory safety or removing Python from the runtime matters: local model serving, agents, search, data pipelines, classical ML, audio, documents and numerical work. It is not yet a replacement for PyTorch research, reinforcement learning, cross-machine training or the broadest model coverage. Use Python there, for model conversion and for some ONNX-heavy paths. The cost that remains is early APIs and wrapper-heavy inference.

jobs.verdict: Local quantized models: [[mistralrs]], [[aha]], [[llama-gguf]]. OpenAI-compatible servers: [[candle-vllm]], [[blazr]], [[shimmy]]. Pure-Rust ONNX: [[tract]], [[oxionnx]], [[rten]], [[lele]]. Limits: early APIs, narrow certified sets, optional Python conversion.

Build agents, MCP tools, provider clients and RAG in Rust. [[adk-rust]] and [[rig]] cover loops, tools and tracing; [[rmcp]] is MCP plumbing; [[async-openai]] covers hosted APIs; [[swiftide]] covers RAG. Limits: early APIs, uneven evaluation depth, and optional Python tooling for some MCP servers.

Train and fine-tune on one GPU with [[burn]], [[candle]] and [[rumus]]; [[oxidizr]] handles checkpoints and one-machine multi-GPU. Limits: cross-machine training is not shown, reinforcement-learning trainers are missing, and [[pmetal]] and [[flodl]] wrap native runtimes.

Local ASR, TTS, VAD, diarization and audio decode work in Rust: [[earshot]], [[speakrs]], [[any-tts]], [[voxr]]. Limits: narrow model sets, fixed mono audio, and wrappers such as [[sherpa-onnx]] and [[whisper-rs]] leave the engine in native code.

Vector and hybrid search are production-grade in Rust with [[qdrant]], [[meilisearch]] and [[tantivy]]; tokenizers are broad with [[tokenizers]] and [[kitoken]]. Limits: local embedding and reranking often still run through ONNX Runtime in [[fastembed-rs]].

Decode and transform images with [[imageproc]]; [[kornia-rs]] adds formats and operators but uses native codecs. [[usls]] covers detection and segmentation through ONNX Runtime. Image generation has a Rust path in [[candle]], while [[diffusion-rs]] wraps a native engine. Limits: maintained object tracking is thin.

[[vidr]] covers decode, model inference on frames, encode and mux, with [[containr]] for MP4 and MKV and [[rav1r]] for AV1. Limits: no VA-API, no AMD or Intel Vulkan Video, no CPU HEVC or VP9 encode, and some CPU codecs wrap native libraries.

OCR and PDF extraction are practical in Rust with [[ocrs]], [[edgeparse]] and [[pdf-oxide]]; layout and office conversion come from [[docling]] and [[oar-ocr]]. Limits: many layout and VLM paths wrap ONNX or native runtimes, and several engines omit OCR or rasterization.

Classical ML, trees, forecasting and explanations work in Rust with [[smartcore]], [[linfa]], [[augurs]], [[perpetual]] and [[treeboost]]. Limits: early APIs, no XGBoost export in [[treeboost]], and [[egobox]] requires Python.

Arrays, linear algebra, FFT, sparse, statistics, optimization and ODE/PDE solvers exist in Rust with [[ndarray]], [[faer]], [[rustfft]], [[statrs]] and [[differential-equations]]. Limits: SciPy parity is uneven, sparse Cholesky is license-gated, and plotting often stays in Python.

Multi-vendor tensor work is real in Rust: [[burn]] and [[cubecl]] compile across CUDA, ROCm, Metal and WebGPU; [[candle]] and [[numr]] cover GPU tensors. Limits: alpha APIs, uneven backend features, and fewer ready ML operations than PyTorch.

Model files, Arrow and Parquet, dataframes, HDF5 and Zarr, and hub access work with [[safetensors]], [[arrow-rs]], [[polars]], [[hdf5-pure]] and [[hf-hub]]. [[oxidizr]] shows a streaming token loader in a Rust trainer. Limits: some HDF5 writers are partial.

use_now.use_for: Production vector and hybrid search server
use_now.why: Rust server with dense, sparse and multi-vector search, filtering, sharding and replication. A team can run it without Python.

use_now.use_for: Full-text and hybrid search behind an API
use_now.why: Single Rust binary with typo tolerance, facets and hybrid search. Sharding and replication need the commercial edition, so plan scale.

use_now.use_for: Arrow and Parquet interchange in Rust services
use_now.why: Official Arrow implementation with IPC, Flight and Parquet work. Many teams build on it.
Rust dataframe engine with lazy queries, streaming and Arrow zero-copy. Python bindings are optional, not required for Rust use.
Broad OpenAI API coverage, streaming, retries and custom compatible endpoints. Teams build on it; some newer API families lack schemas.

use_now.use_for: MCP clients and servers in Rust
use_now.why: Rust MCP SDK with tools, resources, prompts and transports. It is protocol plumbing, not an agent runtime.

use_now.use_for: Tensor math, training and inference in Rust
use_now.why: One codebase across CPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan and WebGPU, with autodiff and NN modules. APIs are early and ONNX import is partial.
Broad tokenizer pipeline with Hub loading, training and tokenizer.json. Python bindings are separate.

use_now.use_for: SafeTensors model file read and write
use_now.why: SafeTensors tensor file read and write with zero-copy tensor reads. It is a safe default for model weights.

watch.why: Runs ONNX with no C or C++ dependency and broad operator coverage. Still early: limited sampling, partial GPU providers and no tokenizer.
Runs small Needle tool models in browser, edge and no_std. Narrow to tool selection, not open chat.
One Rust kernel language compiles to CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan and WebGPU. Alpha, with uneven features and no WebGPU tensor cores.
Covers optimization, ODE/PDE, signal, spatial and statistics on numr. Young and one maintainer; WebGPU is single precision only.

watch.use_for: Video decode, model inference and encode
watch.why: Handles GPU decode, frame tensors, restoration and muxing in Rust. Early: no VA-API, limited codecs and some native CPU decoders.

build_today.goal: Private document Q&A service with local embeddings
build_today.why: Serve an open model locally with [[candle-vllm]], embed documents, store vectors with [[qdrant]] and run retrieval with [[rig]]. All core pieces are maintained.
build_today.watch_out: Fastembed uses ONNX Runtime; model conversion and good chunking still need care.

build_today.goal: Local meeting transcription and speaker review app
build_today.why: Transcribe, detect speech, diarize and decode audio in Rust. A practical local product without Python at runtime.
build_today.watch_out: Inputs are often fixed-rate mono, model sets are narrow, and diarization quality varies.

build_today.goal: Rust tabular forecasting and anomaly service
build_today.why: Classic models, time-series forecasts, boosted trees and explanations can ship as one Rust service. No Python runtime required.
build_today.watch_out: No XGBoost export in treeboost; model formats and APIs are still early.

build_today.goal: On-device PDF and scan intake pipeline
build_today.why: Extract PDF text, tables and reading order, then OCR scans. Rust paths cover most intake without a Python service.
build_today.watch_out: OCR and layout model coverage is uneven; some paths wrap ONNX Runtime or omit rasterization.

holes_filled.hole: Local OpenAI-compatible LLM serving without Python
holes_filled.note: Teams can ship a local API server in Rust. Early APIs and certified model lists are the limits; conversion scripts may still use Python.

holes_filled.hole: Agent apps with provider clients and MCP tools
holes_filled.note: Loops, tools, MCP and hosted APIs are available in Rust. Python can go for core runtime; some MCP servers still launch via Python tools.
Search infrastructure and tokenization can run in Rust. Python is not needed for search serving; embedding wrappers may still use ONNX Runtime.

holes_filled.hole: Model file and columnar data I/O
holes_filled.note: Weights, GGUF, Arrow and Parquet are covered. Python can go for storage and dataframe work; training-loop loaders are app-specific.

holes_filled.hole: Speech recognition, synthesis and VAD on own hardware
holes_filled.note: ASR, TTS, VAD and diarization run in Rust. Runtime Python can go; one-time model export and vocabulary extraction may not.
Regression, trees, clustering, forecasts and explanations are covered. Python can go for many classic models, not for the full XGBoost ecosystem.

holes_filled.hole: GPU tensor math and custom kernels in Rust
holes_filled.note: Teams can prototype and ship tensor work across vendors without Python. Expect alpha APIs and fewer ready operations than PyTorch.
Text PDFs, tables, reading order and OCR have Rust paths. Some layout and VLM paths still wrap native runtimes.

holes_open.impact: Teams training RL agents cannot stay in Rust for the trainer and must use Python frameworks or build the loop themselves.
holes_open.workaround: Use Python RL libraries, or implement the environment in Rust and train in Python.

holes_open.impact: Teams scaling training beyond one machine have no shown Rust path; only one-machine multi-GPU is covered.
holes_open.workaround: Use Python distributed training, or one-machine multi-GPU with [[oxidizr]] or [[rumus]].

holes_open.hole: Maintained object tracking and motion analysis
holes_open.impact: Video analytics teams needing multi-object tracking must build it or leave Rust; the tracker row is unmaintained.
holes_open.workaround: Use Python trackers, or build SORT-style logic on [[kornia-slam]] motion primitives.

holes_open.hole: Full ONNX operator and GPU parity in pure Rust
holes_open.impact: Arbitrary exported models may fail on [[tract]] or [[oxionnx]], forcing a wrapper or Python.
holes_open.workaround: Use [[ort]] when coverage matters, or convert models to Burn with [[burn-onnx]].

holes_open.hole: VA-API and AMD or Intel Vulkan Video decode
holes_open.impact: Linux video teams on AMD or Intel GPUs cannot rely on the Rust video path for hardware decode.
holes_open.workaround: Use [[vidr]] on NVIDIA or CPU paths, or keep a native pipeline.

holes_open.impact: Teams need custom logs or Python tools to compare runs across projects.
holes_open.workaround: Use [[oxidizr]] checkpoints for its own loop, or export metrics to an external tracker.

charts.takeaway: Much of the work still happens in wrapped native code rather than pure Rust, so interop and portability remain core design concerns.
GPU acceleration is uneven and frequently undocumented, so teams must validate backend support before committing.
Recent releases are common, indicating active maintenance, but stale projects remain enough to require due diligence.
